newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen boosted after rise on LIFFE.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen boosted after rise on LIFFE.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to edge upwards on Monday, retaining upward momentum from a rise on LIFFE on Friday, traders said.
They are also likely to receive support from a rise in U.S. Treasuries and receiving of short-term fixed interest rates by Japanese banks on Friday, a trader at a trust bank's securities unit said.
There is some focus on revised industrial output data for April due at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT), the trader said. An upward revision may invite some selling, he said.

"But even if there is an upward revision of the output data, the selling is unlikely to last long. Demand for JGBs will probably emerge on dips and provide support," the trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
The government's preliminary figures released in May showed Japan's industrial output fell 0.4 percent in April.
The September ended at 124.10 on LIFFE, up from Friday's Tokyo close of 123.85.
The market's main focus on Monday will be movements in the foreign exchange markets and Tokyo share prices, a trader for another trust bank's securities unit said.
"The biggest factor this week will be movements in the foreign exchange markets ahead of the Denver (G7) summit meeting," the second trader said.
The upside of JGBs may be capped if Tokyo share prices rise after a surge in U.S. share prices on Friday, the first trader said.
The key Dow Industrial average jumped 70.57 points, or 0.9 percent, to end at 7,782.04 on Friday.
A Group of Seven nations meeting is due to be held from June 20 to June 22 in Denver, Colorado.
